text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Netanyahu will ask U.S. President Clinton to send message to Damascus.
- Palestinian Authority confirms its gas tax revenues refunded by Israel into Bank Leumi account.
- Ehud Barak to throw hat into Labour ring today.
- Tender issued for toll section of Trans-Israel Highway.
- Most provident funds suffer negative real yields.
- Union Bank sale won't occur without workers' okay, MI Holdings, state firm in charge of selling the state's bank holdings agrees.
- Israel Electric Corporation chairman Yaacobi: IEC must cope with competition.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Clinton will say to Netanyahu this evening: It is necessary to implement the redeployment in Hebron.
- Indictment against Jerusalem Mayor Olmert.
HAARETZ
- Israel army: the number of those leaving reserve service thousands higher than the number participating.
- Justice Minister Hanegbi supports expulsion of family members of suicide terrorists.
- Anger in Labour on Barak's decision to announce candidacy for party chief when Peres was abroad.
- Sources in Prime Minister's office: thin chances of further cuts in 1996 budget.
- An investigation company will interrogate senior Bank Hapoalim officials for leaks.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu offered Syrian President Assad a summit - and was denied.
- Treasury proposes 40 percent additional salary to mayors.
- Olmert decides: I won't resign.
GLOBES
- Moody's and Standard and Poor's approved renewal of Israel's credit rating.
- Bank Leumi in contacts with South African shareholders to support splitting off of Africa-Israel.
- Estimates: two billion shekels in additional cuts from 1997 budget needed.
